descriptors.R: the sitting President, nominee of the wartime coalition of the administration party and pro-war members of the opposition, pledged to fight on to unconditional surrender and to amend the Constitution to abolish slavery
descriptors.D: nominee of the opposition party, whose platform calls the war a failure and urges immediate efforts toward a cessation of hostilities; a former commanding general of the Union armies, removed in 1862, who says he will not accept peace without Union

compile_desc.R: the wartime Union coalition led by the administration party
compile_desc.D: the opposition party, whose platform calls the war a failure

others_line: Other candidates on very few ballots (answer "other").
never_name: Lincoln, Andrew Johnson, McClellan, Pendleton, Frémont, Grant, Sherman, Jefferson Davis, Vallandigham or Seward

slice_sources.men: 1860 census aged to November 1864, white men 21+ in the loyal states (the eleven seceded states did not vote, and Louisiana's and Tennessee's returns were not counted); many states let soldiers vote in the field; a few New England states let Black men vote; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.women: No women could vote for president in 1864; women 21+ in the loyal states shown for population only.
slice_sources.south-white: The eleven seceded states cast no counted vote in 1864; their white adults (1860 census) are shown for population only and contribute nothing to the result.
slice_sources.black-south: The eleven seceded states cast no counted vote in 1864, and enslaved people could vote nowhere; Black adults in those states (1860 census) are shown for population only.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1860 census aged to 1864, foreign-born white men in the loyal states not yet naturalized; several Midwestern and Western states let declarant aliens vote, elsewhere only naturalized men could.
